newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq moves higher ahead of unemployment report.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq moves higher ahead of unemployment report.

text.p: The Nasdaq Composite Index moved up on Thursday in choppy trade that saw dips in technology leaders Intel Corp and Microsoft Corp.
The Index closed up 3.09 to 1300.11, or 0.24 percent.
"Nasdaq was a mixed bag as far as technology stocks were concerned," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers.
"The overall health is still there. I think rotating (investments) ... is the best way to invest in the market."

He added that traders were focusing on unemployment numbers out on Friday. The government will release November unemployment figures at 0830 EST/1330 GMT, with the consensus estimate that they will remain unchanged at 5.2 percent.
Advancing stocks outpaced falling stocks 2318 to 1966 on unofficial volume of about 618 million shares.
Most-active Intel Corp shares fell 1-1/4 to 128-1/4 on volume of 10.3 million shares. Microsoft Corp also fell, ending down 1/4 to 153.
Integrated Medical Resources Inc fell 2-5/8, or 43.75 percent, to 3-3/8 after Hambrecht & Quist started coverage with a hold rating.
